issues.display_title: Issue #4259: feat(auth): Hidden Keycloak Login Entry Point (?auth=keycloak) + Callback Page
issues.main_description_html:
Ref: GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1860

Summary

Add a hidden Keycloak SSO login entry point (?auth=keycloak) and dedicated callback handler without affecting existing login methods (password & Google).

Implementation Scope

  1. Hidden Entry Point (Login.jsx):
    • Detect ?auth=keycloak query param; standard login UI remains untouched.
    • Generate anti-CSRF state in sessionStorage (kc_state).
    • Auto-redirect to Keycloak OIDC endpoint (response_type=token, implicit flow).
    • Graceful fallback with toast and redirect to /auth if env configs are missing.
  2. Dedicated Callback (KeycloakCallback.jsx):
    • Route: /auth/keycloak/callback (added to publicPages whitelist in App.jsx).
    • Extract #access_token & state; immediately strip URL hash and purge storage state.
    • Verify anti-CSRF state; exchange token via POST /v1/auth/keycloak-login.
    • Fail gracefully with toast and redirect to /auth on error or state mismatch.
  3. Session Completion Helper (completeAuthLogin.js):
    • Shared helper to persist sid in localStorage and redirect to /?token=... across password, Google, and Keycloak.
  4. Analytics & Unit Tests:
    • Track Countly funnel (login_started, login_completed, login_failed).
    • Unit tests for Login redirect and KeycloakCallback flows (Login.countly.test.jsx, KeycloakCallback.test.jsx).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Standard login (/auth) remains unaffected.
  • /auth?auth=keycloak generates CSRF state and redirects to Keycloak SSO.
  • /auth/keycloak/callback bypasses auth guard, sanitizes hash, and exchanges token via API.
  • Invalid state or login failures redirect back to /auth with toast.
  • Successful login establishes dashboard session correctly.
  • Unit tests and production build pass.

Result

issues.display_title: Issue #4278: fix(auth): Fix Keycloak callback state mismatch on password reset
issues.main_description_html:
Ref: #4259

Summary

Fix the state_mismatch login failure on /auth/keycloak/callback when returning from a Keycloak password reset.

Problem

When users reset their password via email, the link opens in a new browser tab where sessionStorage (kc_state) is empty. This caused an unintended state mismatch error even though Keycloak returned a valid access token.

Solution

  1. Cross-Tab State: Persist kc_state in both localStorage and sessionStorage.
  2. Graceful Token Exchange: If expectedState is not found in storage (due to email reset links in new tabs), proceed with token exchange to backend where the token is verified cryptographically.
  3. CSRF Protection: Retain strict state matching when expectedState is present in storage.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Standard login via Keycloak continues to validate anti-CSRF state.
  • Password reset links opened in new tabs successfully log in instead of failing with state mismatch.
  • URL hash is immediately stripped on callback.
  • All unit tests pass and build succeeds.

Result

  • PR: Opened via #4277
  • Tests: KeycloakCallback.test.jsx (7/7 tests pass) and Login.countly.test.jsx (3/3 tests pass).
  • Build: Production build verified with npm run build.

issues.display_title: Issue #4279: feat(profile): integrate granular CRUD APIs for Maps JavaScript API keys
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Integrate the newly created granular RESTful CRUD endpoints from backend (PR GoThruMedia/GoThru-API-New#1871 / Issue #1870) into the Maps JavaScript API management page (src/pages/Profile/MapsJavascript/).

Background

Previously, Maps JavaScript API key management relied on a single legacy bulk synchronization endpoint (POST /users/map-javascript with a maps: [...] payload). With the UI redesign in design/dashboard-maps-api-key-revision moving to modal-based CRUD:

  • Backend has added individual endpoints for create, update, and delete.
  • Frontend should transition from sending the entire array to using these dedicated granular endpoints.

Related Backend Endpoints

  • Create: POST /users/map-javascript
    • Payload: { "name": string, "key": string, "type": "global" | "tour" }
    • Response: 200 OK with created key object { id, name, key, usage_location }
  • Update: PUT /users/map-javascript/{id}
    • Payload: { "name": string, "key": string, "type": "global" | "tour" }
    • Response: 200 OK with updated key object { id, name, key, usage_location }
  • Delete: DELETE /users/map-javascript/{id}
    • Response: 200 OK

Scope of Work

  1. Hook Integration (src/pages/Profile/MapsJavascript/MapsJavascript.jsx):
    • Replace bulk usePost with individual hooks:
      • usePost for Create (/users/map-javascript)
      • usePut for Update (/users/map-javascript/{id})
      • useDelete for Delete (/users/map-javascript/{id})
  2. State Management:
    • Update local state and Redux store based on the granular responses instead of refetching the entire list every time.
  3. Modal Form Handling:
    • KeyFormModal: Trigger create API for new key or update API for existing key.
    • DeleteAPIKey: Trigger delete API with specific key id.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Update MapsJavascript.test.jsx to mock and verify granular POST, PUT, and DELETE requests.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Adding a key sends POST /users/map-javascript with { name, key, type }.
  • Editing a key sends PUT /users/map-javascript/{id} with { name, key, type }.
  • Deleting a key sends DELETE /users/map-javascript/{id}.
  • UI reflects changes immediately with proper toast feedback.
  • Unit tests pass 100%.
